core_concepts: Introduction My Story ON THE FINAL day of my sophomore year of high school, I was hit in the face with a baseball bat
The bat smashed into my face with such force that it crushed my nose into a distorted U-shape
When I opened my eyes, I saw people staring at me and running over to help
My teacher looped his arm around my shoulder and we began the long walk to the nurse’s office: across the field, down the hill, and back into school
When we arrived at the nurse’s office, she asked me a series of questions
“Who is the president of the United States?”
“Patti,” I said casually, ignoring the fact that it had taken me ten seconds to remember my own mother’s name
mechanisms_or_explanations: When I opened my eyes, I saw people staring at me and running over to help
Shocked and confused, I was unaware of how seriously I had been injured
When we arrived at the nurse’s office, she asked me a series of questions
When my mom and I landed on the roof of the hospital, a team of nearly twenty doctors and nurses sprinted onto the helipad and wheeled me into the trauma unit
When I finally regained consciousness, I discovered that I had lost my ability to smell
The ophthalmologist said my eye would gradually slide back into place as the air seeped out, but it was hard to tell how long this would take
I was determined not to let my injury get me down, but there were more than a few moments when I felt depressed and overwhelmed
I became painfully aware of how far I had to go when I returned to the baseball field one year later
When the season rolled around, I was the only junior to be cut from the varsity baseball team
And I knew that if things were going to improve, I was the one responsible for making it happen
The turning point came two years after my injury, when I began college at Denison University
HOW I LEARNED ABOUT HABITS Attending Denison was one of the best decisions of my life

But my return to baseball was not smooth
After a year of self-doubt, I managed to make the varsity team as a senior, but I rarely made it on the field
These improvements were minor, but they gave me a sense of control over my life
As each semester passed, I accumulated small but consistent habits that ultimately led to results that were unimaginable to me when I started
But it was not until my senior season that my sleep habits, study habits, and strength-training habits really began to pay off
important_examples: For example, for the first time in my life, I made it a habit to lift weights multiple times per week, and in the years that followed, my six-foot-four-inch frame bulked up from a featherweight 170 to a lean 200 pounds

In 2015, I reached two hundred thousand email subscribers and signed a book deal with Penguin Random House to begin writing the book you are reading now
In 2016, my articles began to appear regularly in major publications like Time, Entrepreneur, and Forbes
